# schema { #wdm.schema }

`schema`

CSV column definitions and validation.

The schema is deliberately permissive about *missing* values and strict about
*wrong* ones. Missing data is the normal case -- you will skip weigh-ins and
forget to log meals, and the filter is built for exactly that. Silently wrong
data is the dangerous case, because nothing downstream can detect it.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [ValidationReport](#wdm.schema.ValidationReport) | Outcome of validating an observations file. |

### ValidationReport { #wdm.schema.ValidationReport }

```python
schema.ValidationReport(
    errors=list(),
    warnings=list(),
    n_rows=0,
    n_episodes=0,
    n_weights=0,
    n_intake=0,
)
```

Outcome of validating an observations file.

``errors`` block loading; ``warnings`` do not. The distinction is that an
error means the data cannot be interpreted, while a warning means it can be
interpreted but probably should not be trusted without a look.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [validate](#wdm.schema.validate) | Validate a raw observations dataframe. |

### validate { #wdm.schema.validate }

```python
schema.validate(df)
```

Validate a raw observations dataframe.

Checks, in order: required columns present, no unknown columns, dates
parseable and unique within episode, numeric columns numeric and within
plausible bounds, and macronutrients consistent with reported total energy.
